I read the whole file (lines 1–119) and applied only the "Repeated proof machinery" rubric. I did not open the Mathlib sources.

The additivity proofs are `resolutionMap_add`, `cochainsMap_add`, `map_add`, `map_zero` and `map_add_apply`. Each one works at a different level: resolution maps, cochain complexes, homology, the zero morphism, and elementwise evaluation. Each is also a short, direct step from the one before it. There is no block of nontrivial reasoning that appears in two proofs and could be pulled out into a shared lemma.

`map_zero` builds an `AddMonoidHom` from `map_add` and takes `F.map_zero`. `map_add_apply` is a one-line `simp only`. Both are thin uses of existing API, not repeated machinery.

The `coefficientFunctor` proofs (`map_id`, `map_comp`, the `Additive` instance) each appear once and only unfold definitions or call `map_add`. I found no repeated proof machinery.

The remaining uncertainty is that I did not search Mathlib or the other Formal Frontier libraries for similar additivity proofs elsewhere. The rubric only counts repetition within proofs, so this did not affect the verdict.
